incident-bot: INCIDENT detected · service=redwood-inference-runtime · node=inference-23 · symptom=CUDA error: out of memory despite headroom reported. Severity=P1. Pager: Mira P. Link: https://internal/incident/1765432100

Mira P.: I'm on it. seeing a spike of OOMs across ~8 pods on inference-23. Headroom being reported ~2GiB in metrics but runtime logs show allocation failures. Suspect allocator fragmentation / reserved-block misalignment.

Alex T.: noted. grabbing recent logs + nvidia-smi. pls paste the allocator metrics if you have them handy. trying to avoid full node restart if possible.

Sofia L.: pasting short log excerpts, scrubbed:

```
runtime: allocate_allocation failed: CUDA error: out of memory\n... requested=536870912, available_headroom=2254857830\nallocator: cannot find contiguous block size=536870912 in free list
kv_cache: pinned_reserve_blocks=3 pinned_bytes=2147483648
```

nvidia-smi snapshot from pod (timestamp 17:05 UTC):
```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+\n| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |\n| 0   A40              Off       | 00000000:5B:00.0 Off |                    0 |\n+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+\n| Processes:                                                       GPU Memory |\n|  GPU       PID   Type   Process name                             Usage      |\n|    0     12345      C   /opt/runtime/bin/llm_worker               31712MiB   |\n+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

Mira P.: interesting — kernel-level view shows ~31GB used of 40GB, so ~9GB free, but allocator complains it can't find a contiguous ~512MiB chunk. That points to heavy internal fragmentation and pinned reserved blocks.

Raj K.: do we have reserve/evict metrics from rd-agent?

ops-bot: rdctl node show inference-23 --json
```
node: inference-23
  total_gpu_mem: 40960MiB
  reserved_pool: 12288MiB
  kv_cache_reserved: 2048MiB
  active_free: 5120MiB
  sparepool_hold: 8192MiB
  last_compaction: 2025-04-12T16:58:07Z
```

Raj K.: ok reserved_pool 12GB + kv cache 2GB + sparehold 8GB = fragmentation islanding free memory into many small slots. Headroom metric is computed as total_free - reserved but not accounting for contiguous requirement. So headroom is misleading here.

Sofia L.: this matches earlier reproduction where prefetch pinned a few 1GB blocks. If a newer model loads and requests >1 contiguous GB, it'll fail even with headroom shown.

Alex T.: temporary mitigation options:
- disable KV prefetch / reduce kv_cache_reserved on this node
- trigger allocator compaction if supported (rdctl node compaction)
- drain/cordon node and rolling restart (slow, impacts throughput)

Mira P.: trying compaction first. rdctl node trigger-compaction inference-23

ops-bot: command accepted, compaction started (async). ETA ~45s.

(45s later)

Mira P.: compaction completed — seeing immediate drop in allocation failures for 2 minutes, then OOM spike resumed. looks like compaction freed small fragments but new allocations/pinning re-created holes.

Alex T.: going to flip runtime flag to disable async KV prefetch on the node to avoid new pinned blocks. Patch to daemonset env: RUNTIME_KV_PREFETCH=false for pods on inference-23.

Mira P.: good call. Alex, can you patch the node via label selector so only pods on inference-23 pick it up?

Alex T.: yep. running:
```
kubectl patch ds inference-runtime -n inference --type=json -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/-","value":{"name":"RUNTIME_KV_PREFETCH","value":"false"}}]' --selector=topology.kubernetes.io/hostname=inference-23
```

ops-bot: patch applied. rollout started for pods on node inference-23. 4/8 pods restarted.

Mira P.: monitoring. metrics -> allocation_failures rate dropped by ~80% within 30s after second pod restarted.

Sofia L.: customer impact check: initial surge impacted ~18 tenants (short tails, increased latency and a small number of 500s). Current impact down to 2 tenants with single-request errors.

James H.: good mitigation. follow-ups we should capture: allocator should expose contiguous-free metric not just headroom. Also consider forced coalescing compaction on reserve free lists when fragmentation > threshold.

Raj K.: agreed. I'll keep the node under watch and coord with infra for a full postmortem. For now I recommend leaving RUNTIME_KV_PREFETCH disabled on this node until we patch allocator.

Mira P.: handoff — I need to go off-call in 10m. @Raj K. you're the active oncall; please take lead. Summary in the incident doc: rapid OOMs due to fragmentation + pinned reserve blocks; compaction and disabling kv prefetch reduced errors; customers mostly recovered.

Raj K.: taking handoff. I'll escalate to infra for longer-term plan (allocator coalescing, reserve tuning). I'll also schedule controlled drain+recreate if we see flapping again.

incident-bot: UPDATE · status=monitoring · affected_tenants=2 · mitigation=kv_prefetch_disabled+compaction · start_ts=1765432100 · update_ts=1765432300

Mira P.: quick ops note for post-incident: run a stress test that loads many small allocations then attempts large contiguous allocations to reproduce. Add automated alert when contiguous_free < request_threshold to avoid misleading headroom.

James H.: adding to backlog: ALLOC-237 "contiguous free metric + compaction policy". assign @eng-runtime.

ops-bot: rdctl alert create --node inference-23 --name "contiguous_free_low" --threshold 600MiB --action notify-sre

Raj K.: I'm leaving the node in patched state; if we see any regressions I'll trigger drain. wrapping handoff details into the incident doc now.

Mira P.: thanks all. I'll post a short postmortem tomorrow with timeline & customer comms draft. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT update · resolved=false · monitoring=true · last_update=1765432350
